lessonRef.focus: one no or infinitely many solutions
lessonRef.title: Discussion or problem seminar: one no or infinitely many solutions

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One approach is shown. There is at least one other that works.

items.prompt: Classify the system: y = 2x + 3 and y = 2x - 1. Does it have one solution, no solution, or infinitely many solutions?

steps: Both equations have the same slope, 2, so the lines are parallel.
The y-intercepts are different (3 and -1), so the lines never meet.
A system of parallel, non-identical lines has no solution.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: For each, name a second method before you solve it.

items.prompt: The reference equation is y = -6x + 17. Which of these equations, paired with the reference, would give the system infinitely many solutions?
Plan A charges a $92 flat fee plus $6 per month. Plan B charges a $66 flat fee plus $8 per month. After how many months do the two plans cost the same, and what is that cost?
Plan A charges a $115 flat fee plus $9 per month. Plan B charges a $99 flat fee plus $11 per month. The solution to the system is (8, 187). What does this solution represent?
choices: Plan A costs $187 more than Plan B after 8 months.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: System: y = 7x - 94 and y = -9x + 114. Does the point (13, -3) satisfy both equations, fail one, or fail both?
Plan A charges a $38 flat fee plus $10 per visit. Plan B charges a $42 flat fee plus $6 per visit. The solution to the system is (1, 48). What does the y-coordinate of the solution represent?
choices: The shared cost, in dollars, when the two plans are equal.
The rate Plan B charges per visit.
The difference in cost between the two plans.
The number of visits after which the two plans cost the same.

items.prompt: System: y = x - 16 and y = -9x + 24. Which point (x, y) satisfies both equations?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Argue for one method over another. Say what makes it better, not just that it is.

items.prompt: Solve the system: y = -8x - 139 and y = 9x + 133. What is the intersection point (x, y)?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Relationship A: x: -8, -7, -6, -5 y: -22, -17, -12, -7. Relationship B: x: -8, -7, -6, -5 y: -14, -13, -12, -11. At which x-value do the two relationships have the same y-value?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
